tasks.short: Keep student records complete against the required rules

steps.what: Read class notes that the student records must include
Enter the accurate student records in the pupil file
Check the student records are complete against required policies
Confirm the student records meet the administrative regulations

tasks.design: The pupil administration, kept in {OTHER}, shows the required fields for attendance, mark and date. A check lists what is missing before the teacher confirms that version. The teacher still reads the class notes, and the check does not score the pupil.
tasks.previous_blocker: The required fields live in a policy document, and the teacher discovers a gap only when the office sends the record back.
tasks.enabler_now: The pupil file already has those fields, so a missing attendance, mark or date can be listed before the record is confirmed.
tasks.still_hard: The mark and the note still come from the class. A complete form can still hold a wrong mark.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher is the person who saw the work and who confirms that the record is the one that stands.

ambition.what: Whether a student record is complete against the required fields before it is saved, on ordinary days as well as when the office asks.

tasks.altitude: The teacher still reads the class notes and still confirms the official record. Missing fields show before that confirmation. No new right to change a mark rule or to send the record out.

reach.learn: Which required fields the office still sends back.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys keeps pupil records, a support-plan module and learning-goal tracking. No AI is named for that record.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes, sets the education level or watches tests is high-risk. This check only tests that fields are present.
In schools the works-council act does not apply. Staff consent to tools that can monitor them, and parents and pupils have a say on pupil-data rules.

assumptions: The pupil file holds pupil, date, attendance, mark and note. The school policy names which of those are required. A paper mark book is typed once inside the enter step, and that time stays there.
The completeness check tests only that the required fields are present. It does not score the pupil, label the teacher, or infer health.
The teacher confirms the version with pupil, date, attendance, mark and note. The record is not official until that confirmation. A later correction voids it.
The record does not rank teachers by how fast they enter it.
Test the pupil administration's own required-field settings before custom code.
Staff and parent consultation applies because the file holds pupil data. The build days include that.
unknowns: Which fields this school's policy treats as required on an ordinary lesson day.
research_questions: Does the pupil administration already warn on an empty required field, or is that warning only in a separate office report?

already_counted.description: Read back the line just entered against the class notes.
Look at each missing-field flag before confirming.
Confirm the version that will stand as the record.

incremental.description: Update the required-field list when the policy changes, and clear a flag that is wrong.

approvals.approved_version: draft student record with pupil, date, attendance, mark and note, after completeness flags

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A fortnight of handwritten mark books where the required fields are not a fixed list, so the teacher still types every line and still reads every record before confirming it.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enforce the rules that govern students

steps.what: Find the administration policies and rules that govern students
See what the students did before enforcing the rules
Enforce the rules with the students in the room
Write the incident the policies require for these students

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store opens the named rule when the teacher asks for it. The incident note, if the policy requires one, is a short form in the pupil administration {OTHER}. The teacher still sees the incident and still decides the response in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rule text sits in a handbook, and in the moment the teacher relies on memory.
tasks.enabler_now: A named policy can be opened on the phone, and an incident form can offer the fields the policy already lists.
tasks.still_hard: What the pupil did, and what response fits, is only clear to the person in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees the pupils and carries the response. A rule text does not decide it.
tasks.altitude: The teacher still enforces the rules in the room and still writes the note. The rule text is easier to open. No new right to sanction, and no system watches the pupil.

reach.learn: Which incidents the policy says the teacher must write down, and which move to the administrator.

evidence.claim: The response to a pupil in the room stays with the teacher who can see what happened. A stored rule text does not choose the response. Model knowledge.
Inferring pupils' emotions is a prohibited AI practice. This design does not watch pupils or infer how they feel.

assumptions: The policy file holds a rule name, the behaviour it covers, and whether an incident note is required. A paper handbook stays a manual read inside the find step.
The teacher decides the response in the room. Exclusion and formal suspension are an administrator's task, not this one.
There is no camera, no emotion inference, and no score of the pupil's behaviour. The incident note stores what the teacher writes.
The form does not rank teachers by how often they write a note.
Upkeep is keeping the opened rule matched to the current policy text.
unknowns: Which everyday incidents this school's policy requires the teacher to write down.
research_questions: Is the current rule text already a named document, or only a printed handbook?

already_counted.description: Read the opened rule before responding.
Check the incident note against what happened in the room.

incremental.description: Point the lookup at the current policy when the text has changed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of the day the rule is one the teacher already knows, and the response is a conversation in the room, so the lookup is skipped and the enforcement stays in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with parents and staff to resolve student problems

steps.what: Gather marks and notes on the students' academic problems
Draft points on the behavioral and academic problems

loop.purpose: Draft talking points from the teacher's note and the stored marks.
loop.input: Pupil, date, note text, mark and subject.
loop.output: Talking points, each citing a note sentence or a mark.
loop.check: Code rejects a point with no note or mark citation. The teacher rejects a point the note does not mean, and rejects a diagnostic label.
loop.stop: No note on the record, two drafts fail the check, or the teacher rejects the list.
loop.why_not_simpler: The teacher's note is free text and mixes the incident with the academic concern.

steps.what: Confer with parents, guardians, teachers, counselors and administrators
Resolve the students' problems in that conference

tasks.design: The pupil file in {OTHER} opens the marks and the teacher's own notes for the pupil. A draft lists talking points that each cite a note or a mark, and the teacher rejects a point the note does not support. The conference with parents, guardians and colleagues stays in the room, and the draft is not sent out.
tasks.previous_blocker: The notes and marks sit in different places, and the teacher rebuilds the story from memory on the way to the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: The note and the mark are already stored, and a draft can be checked against those two and no other source.
tasks.still_hard: The parent conversation, and what to try next, depend on the people in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher and the parent hear each other. A brief does not resolve the problem.

ambition.what: Whether a talking point cites a mark or a note the teacher already wrote, before the conference, including problems that now have no brief.

tasks.altitude: The teacher still holds the conference and still agrees what to try next. A brief can be ready when a note exists. No new right to diagnose a pupil or to message the parent.

reach.task: Follow up behavioural problems after a parent conference
reach.learn: Which problems had no note the teacher could cite.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys keeps pupil records and learning-goal tracking, which is where the marks and notes for a brief are read from.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk. A point that adds a judgement beyond the teacher's note would sit in that area.
Inferring pupils' emotions is prohibited. The brief does not label how a pupil feels.
Parents and pupils have a say on pupil-data rules, and staff consent to tools that can monitor them.

assumptions: The brief uses the teacher's note and the stored mark. Fields are pupil, date, note text, mark and subject. A problem that was only spoken, with no note, stops the draft.
Each point must cite a note sentence or a mark. The teacher rejects a point that adds a judgement or a diagnostic label. The draft is not the record of the conference.
The draft is not sent to the parent. The teacher speaks in the meeting. Agreed next steps are written by the teacher after the meeting, in the resolve step.
The brief does not infer health. If a note already contains health information, it stays the teacher's words.
This task does not write a formal support plan. That is a separate process.
Test the pupil file's own note and mark screens before custom code.
unknowns: Whether this school already stores a teacher note against the mark, or only the mark.
research_questions: Are behaviour notes and academic marks in the same pupil file?

already_counted.description: Read the gathered notes before accepting a talking point.
Reject a talking point the note does not support.

incremental.description: Relink a talking point when the mark it cites is corrected.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A month of problems that are only spoken in the corridor, with no note on the record, so the draft is empty and the conference still takes the meeting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with staff to plan lessons from the curriculum

steps.what: Open the approved curricula for the lessons to schedule
Draft lessons following the approved curricula goals

loop.purpose: Draft lesson objectives from the approved curriculum for the named topic.
loop.input: Subject, year, topic note and the curriculum objective list.
loop.output: Lesson objectives, each with an objective code from that list.
loop.check: Code rejects an objective whose code is not in the approved list. The teacher rejects an objective the curriculum text does not state.
loop.stop: No curriculum codes, three drafts fail, or the teacher rejects the list.
loop.why_not_simpler: The topic note is free text and the curriculum is a long list of objectives.

steps.what: Confer with other staff members to plan the lessons
Schedule lessons promoting learning that the staff agreed

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store opens the approved curriculum for the subject and year. A draft lesson outline carries only objective codes from that list, and the teacher rejects an objective the text does not state. Staff still confer on the lessons, and the agreed lessons are placed on the {CALENDAR}. The outline does not name a pupil.
tasks.previous_blocker: The curriculum is a booklet, and the outline is rewritten from memory before each staff meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: The objective codes are a fixed list, so a draft can be rejected when a code is not in that list.
tasks.still_hard: What this class needs next is decided by the staff who teach them, in the meeting.
tasks.human_edge: The staff know the class. A draft objective is not the lesson they agree.

ambition.what: Whether a lesson objective carries a code from the approved curriculum, before the staff conference, including lessons now planned from memory.

tasks.altitude: The teacher still confers with colleagues and still agrees the lessons. An outline with curriculum codes can be on the table first. No new right to change the curriculum or to score a pupil.

reach.task: Review whether planned lessons follow the curriculum
reach.learn: Which lesson objectives the staff rejected because the curriculum did not state them.

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts a class activity from a lesson goal. The teacher accepts or changes it.
A pilot suggests arithmetic lessons that the teacher accepts or changes. It does not report time saved.

In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers in 68 English secondary schools, a guided drafting aid cut weekly lesson-planning time from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes, and a teacher panel found no quality difference. That is preparation time, not the staff conference.

In a primary-school trial, Oak's Aila cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, covered 7% of lessons, and use declined over ten weeks. Under one in five teachers felt it meaningfully influenced their teaching.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk. This outline does not score a pupil.

assumptions: The curriculum file holds subject, year, objective code and objective text. The producer is the curriculum owner. A paper booklet stays a manual read in the open step.

Each drafted objective must carry a code that exists in that file. The teacher rejects an objective the curriculum text does not state. The curriculum itself is already approved; this task does not approve it.
The outline does not name a pupil and does not score one. The staff conference decides the lessons.
Scheduling writes the agreed lessons onto the calendar. It does not publish them to pupils.
The trial figures are about preparation time. They are not the saving on this task, because the conference stays.
Test the curriculum document's own objective list before custom code.
unknowns: Whether this school's curriculum is stored as objective codes, or only as a printed booklet.
research_questions: Who is allowed to place a lesson on the shared calendar after the staff meeting?

already_counted.description: Check the opened curriculum is the approved one for this year.
Reject an objective the curriculum text does not state.
Place the agreed lessons on the calendar and read them back.

incremental.description: Relink an objective when its curriculum code changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A term of meetings where the curriculum is a paper booklet and the staff already know the next topic, so the draft is unused and the conference still takes the hour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher still notes the class, still enforces rules in the room, and still sits with parents and colleagues. A record shows missing fields before it is confirmed, a conference can open on the teacher's own notes, and a lesson outline carries curriculum codes before the staff meeting. No new right to score a pupil, to watch a pupil, or to change the curriculum.
reach: School administrator: which required fields the office still sends back.
Counselor: which behavioural problems had no note the teacher could cite.
Head of department: which lesson objectives the staff rejected because the curriculum did not state them.
skills_to_grow: Reject a record that is missing a required field.
Reject a talking point the note does not support.
Reject a lesson objective the approved curriculum does not state.
role.ambitious_version: Missing fields show before a record is confirmed. A conference opens with points tied to notes the teacher wrote. A staff meeting opens with objectives that carry curriculum codes. The teacher still teaches, still enforces in the room, and still talks to parents.
